fix: (1) Add to the builder AND tdd-engineer personas, in the deliverable requirements: 'a NEW package under go/internal/ must be graduated in the same change — append its pattern line to go/.apicover-enforce AND add an apicover_named_test.go naming every exported symbol; a package that is enforced but unnamed fails the repo-wide gate.' Include the one-line example. (2) Make the floor's message self-serving rather than merely correct: it already names the packages — have it also emit the EXACT two edits (the pattern line to append, and the test skeleton path), so a builder that hits it can comply without re-deriving the doctrine. (3) Consider a cheap pre-build check at the TDD boundary: if the cycle's plan creates a new internal package, assert the enrollment edit is in the plan.
notes: Found via the PR #376 epilogue cause distinguisher — the first halt in this project's history whose cause was readable directly from the digest instead of requiring workspace archaeology. Companion to builder-persona-requires-caller-proof (0.90): both are cases where a MANDATORY house rule lives in operator lore and agents therefore cannot follow it.
summary: Batch-21 HALTED (cycle-1218, identical-fingerprint ceiling) because THREE lanes' build phases aborted on the same cause: a new internal package absent from go/.apicover-enforce. The build-handoff floor correctly refuses, but the requirement appears nowhere in the builder's or TDD engineer's brief — so every cycle that adds a package burns a build phase discovering it. Console hit the SAME class twice on 2026-07-30 independently (RunConsoleLease uncovered → CI red on PR #372; ./internal/plane unenrolled → CI red on the same PR), which is strong evidence the gap is in the INSTRUCTIONS, not in any agent's competence. Note ADR-0069's two-apicover-gates distinction: per-cycle ACS coverage and the repo-wide enforce list are different gates, and only the second needs the enrollment line.
title: New internal packages must be enrolled in .apicover-enforce — the requirement is invisible to builders and costs a whole build phase each time
